case.summary: Verdict: fraud at probability 0.90. Customer C08299 denied a $30.02 online purchase (transaction 3581141, product code S) placed from a billing region (203.0) where the card has only one prior visit ever against a modal region of 441.0; the episode is this single transaction, so exposure is $30.02. The decisive evidence is the customer's denial itself (family: customer; historically 4,665/4,665 such denials on this dataset were confirmed fraud) combined with the case-memory calibration score of 0.86 on this transaction (family: memory), well above its real-time risk_score of 0.28; region rarity and the failed R7 recurring-charge test (only 4 same-amount purchases, median gap 55.98 days, outside the 5-35 day window) corroborate rather than drive the call. The one legitimacy-leaning fact is that $30.02 sits comfortably inside the card's normal $49.97-median spending, so an alternative reading is that this is a small, forgotten legitimate charge the customer mistakenly disputed rather than true card-not-present fraud, but the policy's zero-clearance history on denials and the high cms_p outweigh that. No evidence request was made or needed; nothing was assumed beyond the standard denial-floor treatment. The bank should open the case and block the card at the L1 (team-lead) route, per R2, given exposure of $30.02 is well under the $2,500 L1 ceiling; similar closed cases in this same region (CC-5153, CC-3044, CC-4574) were all confirmed fraud, reinforcing that region 203.0 carries a real fraud base rate for this cardholder.
